cards.explanation: The answer is that He brought them out of Egypt. God says, “I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.” He tells them who He is and what He's done before He says a single command. Introductions first, instructions second. I like that order, friends.

The first thing God tells Israel is to have no other gods before Him. He says, “You shall have no other gods before Me.” No second place, no backup, no spare one tucked in the cupboard, friends. It's the very first command out of His mouth.

The answer is an idol of anything in heaven or earth. God says, “You shall not make for yourself an idol in the form of anything in the heavens above, on the earth below, or in the waters beneath.” Sky, land, sea, He covers all three, friends. Nothing is left out, so there's no loophole to hunt for.

The word is jealous. God says, “for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God…” (Exodus 20:5). He says it right after telling them not to bow down to idols or worship them. He doesn't want to share the spot, friends. Nice and clean, just like a good stamp.

The statement is True. God speaks of “…showing loving devotion to a thousand generations of those who love Me and keep My commandments.” Look at the numbers, friends. Just before that, He says “…the third and fourth generations…” for those who hate Him. A thousand is a LOT more than four.

The answer is False. God says, “…for the LORD will not leave anyone unpunished who takes His name in vain.” So the statement on the card has it backward. It's a serious line, friends, and God means it.

The two words are seventh and work. God says, “…but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God…” Six days for labor, then the seventh belongs to the LORD. On that day God says, “…you must not do any work…” For one whole day, friends, the to-do list gets put down.

The statement is True. God says that on the Sabbath you must not do any work, “…neither you, nor your son or daughter, nor your manservant or maidservant or livestock…” The livestock is right there in the list, friends. Even the animals get the day.

The reason God gives is that He made everything in six days and rested on the seventh. He says, “For in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth and the sea and all that is in them, but on the seventh day He rested.” That's the reason He gives for the Sabbath, friends. It points all the way back to creation.

The reason is so their days may be long in the land. God says, “Honor your father and mother, so that your days may be long in the land that the LORD your God is giving you.” This command comes with its reason attached, friends. And the land is something the LORD is giving.

The statement is False. The Sabbath comes with a reason in verse 11, and honoring parents comes with one in verse 12. But these four stand alone: “You shall not murder.” “You shall not commit adultery.” “You shall not steal.” “You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.” God just says them, short and plain, friends.

The things belong to your neighbor. God says, “You shall not covet your neighbor’s house.” and the list ends with “…anything that belongs to your neighbor.” Wanting what's on the neighbor's side of the fence is the thing He names. Eyes on your own cookie tray, friends.
The answer is False. The text says, “…they trembled and stood at a distance.” Nobody rushes closer to the thunder and the smoke, friends. Honestly, I can't picture it going any other way.

The people ask that Moses speak to them instead of God. They tell Moses, Israel's leader, “Speak to us yourself and we will listen…” Then they add, “But do not let God speak to us, or we will die.” They want Moses between them and God's voice, friends.

The statement is True. Moses, Israel's leader, replies, “Do not be afraid…” The people had just said they might die if God spoke to them, so Moses has something to answer. He then tells them, “For God has come to test you, so that the fear of Him may be before you, to keep you from sinning.”

The word is sinning. Moses, Israel's leader, says God has come to test them, “…so that the fear of Him may be before you, to keep you from sinning.” Staying out of sin is the goal he names, friends. It's Moses' own explanation.

The answer is False. The people stood at a distance, but Moses, Israel's leader, “…approached the thick darkness where God was.” Everybody else is holding their ground and he's walking toward it, friends. That's the picture the verse gives.
